selection_rationale: CAND-2026-001 directly targets the core unresolved operational question (LLM→config correctness vs deterministic verifiers), has strong reviewer support (verdict: pass), is experimentally falsifiable, feasible within the stated compute budget, and maps cleanly to the CNSM Agentic track’s reliability/validation focus.
unresolved_uncertainties: UQ1: Degree to which LLM-generated configs satisfy formal network invariants across realistic topologies and vendor constraints (evidence limited)
UQ2: Which standardized metrics validly capture operational correctness/safety for LLM-driven NetOps beyond syntactic measures
UQ3: Effectiveness of bounded iterative self-repair specifically for complex multi-device and policy-level NetOps faults
required_repairs_before_preregistration: Specify deterministic verifier (e.g., Batfish) exact version, parser/ingestion pipeline, and explicit failure-handling for unparsable LLM outputs
Declare exact hosted LLM identifier(s), API settings (temperature/top-p), seed policy, prompt templates (generation and any repair prompts), and enforce model-call budget

Provide concrete sources and selection criteria for vendor templates and topology generation; define rules for creating or omitting gold-reference configurations and how ambiguous intents will be labeled
Preregister retry policy and exclusion criteria (e.g., persistent syntax errors), and document logging/retention of all raw artifacts and verifier logs for reproducibility
